cases.name: http_500_without_retry
cases.observation: With retry and error handling disabled, the HTTP node exposed status 500 as normal output and the workflow succeeded.

cases.name: http_500_with_three_retries
cases.observation: The initial request plus three whole-node retries applied the side effect four times.

cases.name: human_input_resume_after_api_restart

after_approve.error: Aborted: Client response stream closed before app execution completed

cases.observation: The persisted form survived an API-container restart and resumed the graph, but the original debugger response stream did not reconnect.

cases.name: api_kill_is_not_executor_kill
cases.observation: Execution continued in the worker. Restarting the blocked sink produced an HTTP 502, which the no-retry/no-error-strategy workflow still treated as success.

cases.name: worker_kill_after_effect_before_http_response
cases.observation: In this Dify 1.16.1 debugger run, a hard worker crash did not duplicate the side effect in the bounded observation window, but it also did not recover the run; the database snapshot still showed running.

runtime_notes: The workflows were run as unpublished debugger drafts.
The sink fsyncs each event before replying and can block after apply to create a deterministic crash window.
This file is a curated summary; exact event and database rows are preserved in evidence/dify-raw-snapshot.json.
The worker-crash result is a bounded single-run observation, not a proof that no delayed recovery can ever occur.
The local HITL draft required replacing an invalid delivery-method id with a UUID in the Dify draft workflow row.
